Elena — thanks for the countersigned SOW, and great question. High level proposal below; happy to adjust based on AcmeCloud AP preferences.

Proposed billing flow (recommended for committed prepay):
- Activation invoice: 30% of committed amount, issued on countersign (this gets Redwood set up and is what most enterprise AP teams prefer).
- Monthly drawdown invoices: the remaining 70% split across 11 monthly drawdown invoices tied to usage windows (monthly ledger entries, not per-call).
- Final reconciliation: a one-line credit/debit adjustment after month 12 if actual consumption differs from committed spend.

Why this approach: it balances ACME's desire to stage payment with Redwood's need to cover activation costs, and it keeps monthly accounting tidy. If AcmeCloud prefers a 50/50 initial/remaining split we can update the schedule.

VAT / tax evidence we will provide:
- Supplier tax ID and Redwood EU VAT registration (where applicable)
- Formal invoice PDF with VAT line items (country-level)
- VAT evidence checklist (attach) for reverse-charge cases — includes copy of SOW, PO number, supplier registration, and any requested AP forms.

I attached an initial invoice timetable (redwood_invoice_schedule_v1.xlsx) and our VAT evidence template (vat_evidence_template.pdf). Please confirm if the proposed cadence (activation + 11 monthly draws) works for your AP team and whether they need Redwood to issue the activation invoice as "net 14" or "due on receipt".

I can also run a 20-minute call Wednesday 2026-09-04 at 11:00am PST to walk the AP lead through the schedule and tax items — is Keegan available then?

DocuSign / payment links: https://app.docusign.com/rooms/acme-sign — I will add the payment remittance instructions once AP confirms bank preferences.

Attachments: redwood_invoice_schedule_v1.xlsx; vat_evidence_template.pdf

Best,
Connor O'Brien

4) Payment terms: Elena asked whether activation invoice can be net 14 or due on receipt. I'd prefer to set activation as net 14 to help cash flow for larger deals, but we can mark due-on-receipt if legal wants.

Connor
